inputSummary.techNotesSent:
TIME ENTRY WRITE-UPS:
Threat Details

Product: SentinelOne
Threat Status: MITIGATED (Killed + Quarantined)
AI Confidence: MALICIOUS
Classification: Malware (Static Detection)
File: Memo.pdf (69.68 KB)
Path: \Device\HarddiskVolume3\Users\Brianna\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Olk\Attachments\ooa-e54322e1-8499-4d64-a842-010455c45ad7\85693b5e774822087c6bd15b545167c48ba450f105ad298a12c6ebfccc7d2f62\Memo.pdf
Originating Process: msedgewebview2.exe
SHA256: (Add full hash here once available)
Endpoint: DESKTOP-75LRG39 (Windows 10, Brianna)

Root Cause / Analysis
The detection occurred shortly after Brianna opened her laptop. Microsoft Outlook (running in the background or on startup) processed a PDF attachment named Memo.pdf using its embedded Edge WebView2 engine.
This created/accessed the temporary attachment file, which was flagged by SentinelOne’s static analysis. This is a common false positive pattern with Outlook attachment previews and WebView2 cache files. No malicious behavior, network activity, or other indicators were present.
Actions Taken

Threat successfully mitigated by SentinelOne.
Recommended downloading the file for VirusTotal scan.
Advised adding hash exclusion once confirmed clean.
Endpoint remains clean (0 unmitigated threats).

Resolution
False Positive – Legitimate Microsoft Outlook PDF attachment processing via WebView2. No evidence of actual malware.

aiFlags.summary: Confirmed phishing attack at company 594 where multiple users clicked a malicious link and entered credentials from a compromised vendor email.
reasons: Multiple users (Colin Stewart, Gavin Latham, and others) confirmed to have entered login credentials on a phishing page
The phishing email originated from a compromised known vendor, indicating a supply-chain risk
Confirmation still pending on whether all affected users (Steven Nixon, Tyler Sheats) entered credentials — resolution may be incomplete
aiFlags.notesForExec: Brandon Emby handled the phishing incident well (confirmed via INKY, deleted emails, began password resets), but this is a significant security event: a trusted vendor was compromised, multiple employees entered credentials, and confirmation on all affected users appears incomplete. Recommend executive awareness and verifying all compromised accounts have been fully secured, plus considering notifying the vendor of their compromise.
